newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles council delays $200 mln police bond.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles council delays $200 mln police bond.

text.p: Los Angeles City Council delayed until 1998 a proposed $200 million bond measure for police facilities, saying there is too little information to go to the voters this spring, according to a published report Thursday.
Instead, the council voted to spend $100,000 to hire a consultant who will examine options for replacing LAPD's downtown headquarters, Los Angeles Times reported.
Councilmembers said it would have been impossible to build the necessary political support to get the required two-thirds approval for a bond measure this spring, the Times reported.
